PNU potentiates the neuronal nicotinic α7 receptor by increasing the duration of single-channel openings and that this potentiation requires residues lining a transmembrane cavity.

PNU-induced potentiated channel clusters are formed by a mechanism distinct from the agonist-induced opening of individual α7 receptors, and that the structural determinants of the potentiating effect are located in a cavity within the α7 transmembrane domain.

PNU potentiates neuronal α7 AChR single-channel currents by prolonging channel opening episodes by several magnitudes of order and that this potentiation requires residues within a transmembrane cavity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PNU potentiates α7 by prolonging the duration of agonist-induced channel opening episodes and that this potentiation requires a PNU-binding site located in the transmembrane domain of the receptor.

The main takeaway from our work is that

PNU potentiates the α7 AChR by stabilizing a conformation that is normally only transiently populated during agonist binding and that the structural determinants of potentiation are localized to the channel's transmembrane domains.

PNU-induced potentiated α7 opening episodes are long-lived and can be observed at the single-channel level, suggesting that the molecular mechanism of PNU potentiated channel opening is fundamentally different from that of the wild-type receptor.
